doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
title: Timeline and touring Alabama towns alone
summary: She dates leaving Pensacola and first coming to New Orleans around 1929 and lists the Alabama towns she played solo.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah, people come in and go and get their liquor and drinks and dance, gamble, you know, all that, the gambling thing like that. Oh yeah. And let's see, when did you say you left Pensacola? I left Pensacola, let's see, we married 35, how did he? How much of Michigan, I tell you, 27, 28. I came to New Orleans around about, about 20. My first trip I made here in New Orleans, I was playing with Nighthawk Orchestra in Birmingham, and my sister stayed at taking sick. That's when I went to work on the boat, that's what I'm talking about this boat now. Went to work on the boat in her place that she got able to go back to work. See, that's when she was when she was when she was together. And then, that was in, that was around 29, 29.
You traveled all up in Alabama too?
Where all did you go from Pensacola?
Dothan, Ozark, Makanopi, Kendrick, Reddick, and Montgomery, Selma, Besma.
Which bands would you be with going to all these places? By yourself or with bands? I was by myself.

I worked at the Frolic Theater in Besma. And I played different places all around them towns, white and color. White and color, tan, you know like that, you know, didn't have those bands, you know, just house parties like that, you know.
